findings.failure_mode: A run that writes or pipes to an absolute path outside the allowed roots using the common `cmd <<DELIM > path` form is graded contaminated=null and scored as clean; in host mode this hides writes into the real repository or home directory, the exact case the outside_path check exists for.

findings.description: HEREDOC is compiled with re.S, so `.` in `(?:.*?\n)*?` matches newlines. Each iteration can then end at any later newline, and the group can repeat, which makes the number of ways to tile the remaining text 2^(newline count). When the delimiter word never appears at a line start the engine explores all of them before failing. Triggers are `<<` tokens that are not heredocs inside multi-line Bash commands: `$((1<<n))`, a here-string with a literal (`<<<"word"` matches at the second `<`), or `<<` inside quoted text. strip_heredocs runs on every Bash tool_use input in every transcript of a run.
findings.failure_mode: A single multi-line Bash command with a non-heredoc `<<WORD` and a few dozen lines makes contamination() spin for minutes to hours; the grade step for that trial, and the batch behind it, stall.

findings.description: Heredoc bodies are stripped before the path-word scan on the rationale that written file text is data. But a heredoc is stdin to whatever command precedes it, and the most common agent shapes feed it to an interpreter: `python3 - <<'PY'` (this very script uses that form), `bash <<EOF`, `node - <<JS`, `xargs cat <<EOF`, `while read f; do cat "$f"; done <<EOF`. Absolute paths in those bodies are opened at run time, not written to disk, yet 1.2.2 excludes them from the outside_path check.
findings.failure_mode: In host mode a run that reads files under the real home or repository through an inline Python or bash heredoc is graded clean; in container mode reads of /root, /mnt, /media, /srv the same way go unreported.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip the body only when the heredoc's command line shows a file sink (`>`/`>>` redirect on the operator line, or `tee`/`cat >` as the consumer); otherwise keep scanning the body, or scan stripped bodies with the ABS_WORD rule but skip the known false-positive shapes (`#!/usr/bin/env`, `/path/to/...`). At minimum document the interpreter case as an accepted gap in the header.

findings.description: For Bash the `hidden` check is now HIDDEN_TOKEN only: `HIDDEN`, or lowercase `hidden` adjacent to `/ . _ = -` or followed by `.`+alnum. Ordinary probe shapes fall outside it: a bare word (`grep -rn hidden .`, `rg -i hidden`), a glob (`find . -iname '*hidden*'`, the `*` is not in either character set), and mixed case or camelCase (`Hidden/`, `hiddenTests/`). Before 1.2.4 all of these were flagged. The motivating false positive (prose in a reviewer's heredoc) could have been removed more narrowly.
findings.failure_mode: A run that searches the tree for the literal word hidden, or lists a `hiddenTests` or `Hidden` directory, is no longer marked contaminated.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the substring rule (`"hidden" in strip_heredocs(val).lower()`) to the command text with heredoc bodies removed, and apply HIDDEN_TOKEN only to the heredoc bodies (prose). Make HIDDEN_TOKEN case-insensitive for the adjacency branches.

findings.description: in_quotes decides quoting by parity of all `'` and `"` characters before the word, with no awareness of nesting or escapes. An apostrophe in double-quoted text (`echo "don't" && ls /root`) flips the single-quote parity and the sensitive one-component word is skipped. The rule also skips a sensitive word that is itself the quoted argument: `cd "/root"`, `ls "/home"`, `cd '/root'`, none of which were skipped in 1.2.0 (the header lists only `cd '/root/'` as the accepted gap).
findings.failure_mode: Ordinary quoting or an apostrophe earlier in the command hides a one-component outside path from the contamination check; the regression against 1.2.0 is undocumented except for one shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace parity counting with a small shell-aware scan (shlex.shlex in posix mode or a hand-rolled quote state machine tracking '\'' vs '"' vs escape) that reports whether the word is inside a quoted *string with other text*; treat a word that is the entire quoted argument as a path. Document any remaining accepted shapes in the header list.
